This file reads the raw data files in `data/`, cleans them, merges them by year, and
saves the result in `12_DataSaving.RData`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
source("00_requirements.R")
source("01_funct_DataCleaning.R")
source("03_funct_ProjectFunctions.R")
```

## 1. Read the raw data

**NCES Table 106.10** (education spending and nominal GDP). The table was saved from
Excel as a csv file. The function skips the header rows and the footnotes.

```{r read-nces}
nces <- read_nces_table106("data/tabn106_10.csv")
head(nces)
```

**FRED GDPC1** is quarterly real GDP. The function averages the four quarters of each
year to get annual values.

```{r read-fred}
gdp_annual <- read_fred_annual("data/GDPC1.csv")
tail(gdp_annual)
```

## 2. Keep the years we can use

NCES reports every other year before 1969 and every year from 1969 onward, so we keep
1969-2019 (51 years in a row). The 2018 and 2019 NCES values are NCES estimates.

```{r filter-years}
nces <- filter(nces, year >= 1969, year <= 2019)
all(diff(nces[["year"]]) == 1)   # TRUE means no years are skipped
```

## 3. Merge the two data sets by year

```{r merge}
edu_gdp <- merge(nces, gdp_annual, by = "year")
edu_gdp <- edu_gdp[order(edu_gdp[["year"]]), ]
dim(edu_gdp)
head(edu_gdp)
```

## 4. Check for problems

```{r checks}
colSums(is.na(edu_gdp))        # number of missing values in each column
summary(edu_gdp)
```

## 5. World Bank government spending (supplementary, US only)

The World Bank file gives *government* education spending as a % of GDP for about 250
countries. We keep only the United States. It is a short series, so we only use it as a
comparison.

```{r read-wb}
wb_raw <- read.csv("data/WB_WDI_SE_XPD_TOTL_GD_ZS_WIDEF.csv", check.names = FALSE)
wb_us <- wb_raw %>%
  select_country_years() %>%
  make_data_long() %>%
  filter_us_wb()
wb_us
```

## 6. Save

```{r save}
save(nces, gdp_annual, edu_gdp, wb_us, file = "12_DataSaving.RData")
```
